html:
SMTO-UI-0024 — This model setting needs a whole number

GUID: f61537c4-fc56-4c3d-947b-de4c340be0dd
Slug: ui-integer-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • This model setting only accepts whole numbers, but the value you typed has a decimal part or is far too large. SMTO didn't accept the change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the model and find the setting that has the message under it. The message appears right under the setting that needs a whole number.
  2. Remove any decimal point, for example change 1024.5 to 1024, and keep the number to a sensible size. Settings like token limits count whole items, so fractions and extremely large numbers aren't allowed.
  3. If you're unsure, open its Help and use the Explicit starting value, or turn the switch off. Then select Save for that model. The starting value is a known good whole number, and turning the switch off uses the provider's default.

What success looks like

  • The message under the setting disappears and the model saves.

If it still fails

  • Turn the setting's switch off to use the provider default, and send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO's model setup.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An integer model parameter's input failed Number.isSafeInteger (it has a fractional part or exceeds the browser's safe integer range), so the editor rejected the change.

What this means

  • A field requiring an integer fails Number.isSafeInteger. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A field requiring an integer fails Number.isSafeInteger.

How to diagnose it

  • Check fractional input and the browser's exact integer range in addition to field bounds.

How to fix it

  • In model_configuration.js the input change handler throws ui_integer_invalid for integer-typed parameters when Number.isSafeInteger(value) is false (fractional values, or magnitudes above 9007199254740991). Enter an integer within the parameter's minimum/maximum, or turn the override off.
  • Enter an integer within the field’s advertised bounds and the browser safe integer range.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen value is a safe integer within the advertised limits.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
